title: Files already identifying as Garmin lose manufacturer/product and get no device in Garmin Connect (e.g. TrainerDay)
description:
**Summary**
Activities recorded with TrainerDay upload successfully but Garmin Connect shows no device.
TrainerDay writes a `file_id` that already identifies as Garmin (`manufacturer: garmin`,
`garmin_product: edge_530`) and no `device_info` record at all.

**What happens**
1. `rewrite_file_id_message()` always builds a new `FileIdMessage`, but only sets
   `manufacturer`/`product` when `_should_modify_manufacturer()` is true. For other
   manufacturers (including Garmin) the rewritten `file_id` has **no manufacturer or product**,
   and the serial is replaced with the profile/default serial. The docstring says these files
   are "returned unchanged".
2. The file has no `device_info` for the recording device, so even with the identity intact
   Garmin Connect has no creator device to display.

**Decoded (fitdecode)**
- Original `file_id`: `manufacturer: garmin, garmin_product: edge_530, serial_number: 3987112345`; no `device_info`
- After Fit-File-Faker v2.2.1: `file_id` has only `type`, `time_created` and a replaced serial

**Expected**
Files from manufacturers that aren't rewritten keep their `file_id` identity, and a creator
`device_info` is present so Garmin Connect can show the device.

Related but separate: #80 (COROS DURA `device_info` without a product).

title: device_info messages keep the original (non-Garmin) serial_number after editing — breaks device attribution / Training Effect for Hammerhead Karoo source files
description:
Environment

  • fit-file-faker installed via pip install fit-file-faker (current release as of August 2026)
  • Python 3.12, running in Docker
  • Profile app_type: Custom
  • Source device: Hammerhead Karoo 3
  • Target device: Garmin Fenix 7 Pro Solar (product ID 4375), configured with my watch's real Unit ID as the serial number

Summary

After editing a Karoo-recorded FIT file, the file_id message correctly gets the configured Garmin manufacturer/product/serial_number, but the device_info message for the primary device (device_index=0) gets its manufacturer and product fields rewritten while its serial_number field is left untouched — still containing the Karoo's original (non-Garmin) serial number. This produces an internally inconsistent FIT file: file_id and device_info disagree about the device's serial number.

I believe this is why activities uploaded from Karoo files never get Training Effect / Training Status calculated on Garmin Connect, and why the activity's "Devices & Apps" section is empty in the Garmin Connect UI, even though the same profile/device selection works as expected for the file_id message.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Configure a profile with app_type: custom, targeting a Garmin device (e.g. Fenix 7 Pro Solar, product 4375) with a real Unit ID as the serial number.
  2. Edit a Karoo-recorded .fit file without uploading:
   fit-file-faker /path/to/karoo_ride.fit
  1. Inspect the file_id and device_info messages in the original vs. edited file (I used a small custom FIT parser to dump these fields; happy to share it if useful).

Observed data (device_index=0, the primary/head-unit record)

Field | Original file | Edited file -- | -- | -- file_id.manufacturer | 289 (Hammerhead) | 1 (Garmin) — correctly patched file_id.product | 3 | 4375 — correctly patched file_id.serial_number | 240970090 | 3506959378 (my configured Unit ID) — correctly patched device_info[0].manufacturer | 289 | 1 — correctly patched device_info[0].product | 3 | 4375 — correctly patched device_info[0].serial_number | 240970090 | 240970090 — unchanged, still the Karoo's original serial

Every device_info message for device_index=0 across the whole ride (~30 messages in my test file, presumably one per some periodic interval) shows the same pattern: manufacturer/product patched, serial_number not patched.

Expected behavior

device_info.serial_number for the primary device record should be rewritten to match the configured Unit ID, consistent with what's written to file_id.serial_number.

Additional observation

The peripheral sensor device_info records (e.g. device_index=3, originally a power meter reporting manufacturer=32) also get manufacturer/product rewritten to the Garmin values (1 / 4375), which seems unintended too — a connected sensor shouldn't be relabeled as the watch itself. Not sure if that's in scope for the same fix or a separate issue.

Why this matters

Per Garmin's anti-spoofing changes from December 2023 (referenced in a few other FIT-editing tools' docs/issue trackers), Garmin Connect appears to validate internal consistency of device identity before enabling Training Effect / Training Status calculation and device attribution in the UI. A file_id/device_info serial number mismatch looks like exactly the kind of inconsistency that would trip that validation.

Sample files: [test_modified.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31366761/test_modified.zip)

Note: This issue was created mostly with use of AI - probably better than if I did it myself :)

title: Suspicious behavior on PyPI for fit-tool package
description:
We rely on the `fit-tool` package (which has not been updated since 2022). The package on PyPI (https://pypi.org/project/fit-tool/) was suddenly taken over by an anonymous user named "friendsa" (https://pypi.org/user/friendsa/), and the entire version history was deleted (versions prior and equal to 0.9.13).

A new version was released January 27 (0.9.14), which from my examination appears to be byte-wise identical to 0.9.13. There is as-of-yet no malicious code that I could identify in the package, but the situation appears extremely suspicious, as there's no description of who "friendsa" is, no link to an updated repo, and no explanation for why old versions were deleted. 

Prior to this change, the maintainer was Matt Tucker, the original author of the library (https://pypi.org/user/mtucker/), which can be seen in web archives of the package: https://web.archive.org/web/20240323163834/https://pypi.org/project/fit-tool/

I do not have proof, but am suspicious that this is the first stage of a supply chain attack of some sort.

We should immediately switch to a vendored version of the library as of 0.9.13 to minimize exposure. The latest `main` version of FIT File Faker will not install, since I've pinned the fit-tool dependency to 0.9.13, and that package no longer exists on PyPI any longer. 

This was reported via the PyPI malicious package reporting tool, also.

A bit more research points to this repo: https://github.com/shaonianche/python_fit_tool which appears to be a legitimate fork attempt. @shaonianche, can you please explain why you deleted all versions of the fit-tool package from PyPI? That is a tool that is fairly widely used in the Python ecosystem, and it's likely that action broke many workflows.

title: MyWhoosh uploads fail after a MyWhoosh update
description:
When running a MyWhoosh profile in "monitor" mode, there's a problem when the MyWhoosh application updates.

## Problem description

MyWhoosh saves FIT files by overwriting the same file each time a user clicks the "upload" button after a ride. This file is named something like `MyNewActivity-5.5.0.fit`, where `5.5.0` is the current application version. FIT File Faker's monitor mode can detect when a file is changed, but when the version of the application updates, we run into a problem:

1. Before the update, FIT File Faker creates a file named `MyNewActivity-5.5.0_modified.fit`
2. After update, a new file named `MyNewActivity-5.6.0.fit` is created for the new version
3. FIT File Faker modifies and uploads this, leaving four files in the MyWhoosh data folder: 
    - `MyNewActivity-5.5.0.fit`
    - `MyNewActivity-5.5.0_modified.fit`
    - `MyNewActivity-5.6.0.fit`
    - `MyNewActivity-5.6.0_modified.fit`
4. FIT File faker attempts again to modify and upload `MyNewActivity-5.5.0.fit`, since it's not in the `.uploaded_files.json` file, but Garmin rejects it because it's a duplicate, and this continues in a loop until the user quits the application.

## Potential solution

FIT File Faker should attempt to detect an update (by the presence of a new version numbered FIT file), and rename the original older file to something like `MyNewActivity-5.5.0.fit.bak` so it won't be picked up any longer.

title: Add per-profile serial number configuration with auto-generation
description:
**Feature Request: Add Serial Number and Software Version Configuration to Profiles**

## Current State (on main branch)

Serial numbers are currently preserved from the original FIT file without any customization:

```python
# fit_file_faker/fit_editor.py:172-174
if m.serial_number is not None:
    new_m.serial_number = m.serial_number
```

Software version numbers are hard-coded with values only valid for the Edge 830

```python
# fit_file_faker/fit_editor.py:457-462
creator_message = FileCreatorMessage()
creator_message.software_version = 975
creator_message.hardware_version = 255
builder.add(DefinitionMessage.from_data_message(creator_message))
builder.add(creator_message)
```

This means:
- Files from TrainingPeaks Virtual, Zwift, MyWhoosh, etc. retain their original serial numbers
- This appears to be part of the "validation" Garmin Connect does for activities counting toward challenges, etc. (see #51)
- Serial numbers may be completely missing from some sources (Zwift), or not match the Garmin device being emulated (e.g., random serial on an "Edge 830")
- Users cannot specify custom serial numbers for their profiles, which could be used to match their actual hardware devices (not sure if Garmin tracks this across a user's activities for anything)
- No support for generating realistic Garmin-format serial numbers

## Problem

When a FIT file is modified to appear as a Garmin Edge 830 (or other device), the serial number should ideally match a valid serial number for that device type. Currently:

1. **Inconsistent metadata**: Device is rewritten to Garmin Edge 830, but serial number stays as Zwift/TPV/None/etc.
2. **No user control**: Users cannot specify a custom serial number (e.g., to match their actual Garmin device)
3. **Missing validation**: No format checking or generation for Garmin-compatible serial numbers

## Proposed Enhancement

Add serial number configuration and software version validation to the Profile dataclass with auto-generation support.

### Key Features

1. **Per-Profile Serial Numbers**
   - Add `serial_number: int | None` field to Profile dataclass
   - Optional field (defaults to None = preserve original)
   - Stored in `.config.json` alongside other profile settings

2. **Auto-Generation**
   - Generate realistic Garmin serial numbers when creating profiles
   - Format: 32-bit unsigned integer (typical Garmin range: 3900000000-3999999999)
   - Randomized but deterministic per profile
   - Option to regenerate if user wants

3. **Profile Wizard Integration**
   - Prompt: "Generate serial number for this device? (recommended)"
   - Show generated number with option to customize
   - Allow manual entry of existing Garmin device serial
   - Allow "None" to preserve original serial numbers

4. **FIT Editor Integration**
   - Use `profile.serial_number` if set, otherwise preserve original
   - Apply to both `FileIdMessage` and `DeviceInfoMessage` records
   - Log serial number changes at INFO level for transparency

### Benefits

- **Consistency**: Serial numbers match the emulated device type
- **Realism**: Generated serials follow Garmin's format/range conventions
- **User control**: Users can match their actual Garmin device or use generated values
- **Privacy**: Users can avoid exposing real device serial numbers in shared files

## Implementation Suggestions

1. **Profile Dataclass** (config.py:140-158)
   ```python
   @dataclass
   class Profile:
       name: str
       app_type: AppType
       garmin_username: str
       garmin_password: str
       fitfiles_path: Path
       manufacturer: int | None = None
       device: int | None = None
       serial_number: int | None = None  # NEW FIELD
   ```

2. **Serial Number Generation**
   ```python
   def generate_garmin_serial() -> int:
       """Generate a realistic Garmin device serial number.
       
       Returns a 10-digit number in the typical Garmin range
       (3900000000-3999999999 for modern devices).
       """
       import random
       return random.randint(3900000000, 3999999999)
   ```

3. **Profile Wizard** (config.py:329-402)
   - Add serial number prompt after device selection
   - Default to auto-generation with confirm/customize option
   - Validate manual entries (must be positive 32-bit int)

4. **FIT Editor** (fit_editor.py:172-174)
   ```python
   # Replace current logic
   if self.profile and self.profile.serial_number is not None:
       new_m.serial_number = self.profile.serial_number
   elif m.serial_number is not None:
       new_m.serial_number = m.serial_number
   ```

5. **Migration**
   - Existing profiles default to `serial_number: None` (preserve original behavior)
   - No breaking changes to existing configurations

## Serial Number Format Research

Garmin serial numbers follow specific patterns:
- **Modern devices (Edge, Fenix, etc.)**: 10-digit numbers starting with 39 (e.g., 3912345678)
- **Older devices**: May use different ranges (38xxxxxxxx, 37xxxxxxxx)
- **Format**: 32-bit unsigned integer (max: 4294967295)

Initial implementation can use the 39xxxxxxxx range for all devices, with future enhancement to use device-specific ranges if needed.

## Related Files

- `fit_file_faker/config.py:140-158` - Profile dataclass
- `fit_file_faker/config.py:329-402` - Profile creation wizard
- `fit_file_faker/fit_editor.py:172-174` - Serial number handling in FileIdMessage
- `fit_file_faker/fit_editor.py:280-320` - DeviceInfoMessage handling (may also need updates)

## Additional Context

This enhancement complements issue #58 (supplemental device registry). Together they provide:
- Custom device selection (#58)
- Custom serial numbers (this issue)
- Complete device emulation control for users

The feature should be optional and backward compatible - existing profiles continue to work with original serial number preservation.

title: Add supplemental device registry for modern Garmin devices beyond Edge/Tacx
description:
**Feature Request: Expand Device Support with Supplemental Registry**

## Current State

The profile creation wizard already supports device customization via the `get_supported_garmin_devices()` function (`config.py:81-96`), which filters devices from the `fit_tool` library to only include:
- Devices with "EDGE" in the name (bike computers)
- Devices with "TACX" in the name (trainers)  
- Devices with "TRAINING" in the name (Tacx Training App)

This limits users to ~20-30 older bike computer models from the `fit_tool` library's `GarminProduct` enum, which:
- Has not been updated since FIT SDK 21.x (circa 2019-2020)
- Excludes modern devices released 2021-2026
- Lacks firmware version information

## Proposed Enhancement

Add a supplemental device registry to complement the outdated `fit_tool` enum with modern Garmin devices, similar to how we handle manufacturer code 331 (MyWhoosh) which isn't in `fit_tool`.

### Key Features

1. **Supplemental Device Registry**
   - `GarminDeviceInfo` dataclass with metadata: name, product_id, category, year_released, firmware version, etc.
   - Registry of 40-50 modern devices (2019-2026) from FIT SDK 21.188.00
   - Categories: bike_computer, multisport_watch, running_watch, trainer
   - Firmware versions sourced from gpsinformation.net or official Garmin sources

2. **Enhanced Device Picker**
   - Two-level picker: show common devices first, "View all devices" for full catalog
   - Merge fit_tool devices + supplemental registry
   - Display device metadata (year, category, description)
   - Support custom numeric product ID entry

3. **Device Categories to Add**
   - Modern bike computers: Edge 1050, 1040, 840, 540 (2021-2025)
   - Multisport watches: Fenix 8, Fenix 7, Epix Gen 2 (2021-2025)
   - Running watches: Forerunner 965, 955, 265, 255 (2022-2025)
   - Other: Modern Tacx trainers with updated firmware

### Benefits

- Users can emulate their actual Garmin device for more accurate representation
- Better compatibility with Garmin Connect's platform-specific features
- Future-proof design allows easy addition of new devices as they're released
- Improves Training Effect calculations for device-specific algorithms

## Implementation Suggestions

1. Create `SUPPLEMENTAL_GARMIN_DEVICES` dict in config.py
2. Add `get_supported_garmin_devices(show_all=False)` with filtering logic
3. Update profile wizard to use two-level picker
4. Include firmware version in Profile dataclass (optional, for future use)
5. Add CSV reference file: `docs/reference/FitSDK_21.188.00_device_ids.csv`
6. Document firmware extraction process for future updates

## Device Data Source

- **Product IDs**: FIT SDK 21.188.00 (latest as of 2024)
- **Firmware versions**: http://gpsinformation.net/allory/test/garfeat_index.htm

## Related Files

- `fit_file_faker/config.py:81-96` - Current `get_supported_garmin_devices()` function
- `fit_file_faker/config.py:140-158` - Profile dataclass (may need firmware version field)
- `fit_file_faker/config.py:329-402` - Profile wizard device customization section
- `fit_file_faker/fit_editor.py:173-187` - Device rewriting logic (already supports custom devices)

## Additional Context

The infrastructure for custom device simulation already exists:
- Profile dataclass has `manufacturer` and `device` fields

This enhancement just needs to expand the available device catalog beyond the limited `fit_tool` enum.

title: Garmin Connect doesn't recognize MyWhoosh activities as Garmin device – potential fix
description:
First of all, thank you for this excellent project — it’s been extremely useful and works great! In fact, I’ve just submitted a pull request to the project earlier today.

I wanted to share a small observation that might be considered for improvement. When processing FIT files generated by the MyWhoosh training platform, I noticed that they include metadata indicating the device as a Garmin Edge 1030 Plus along with some serial number. However, Garmin Connect doesn’t seem to recognize these activities as recorded with a genuine Garmin device — the device is not displayed in the activity details.

As a workaround, I found that explicitly adding below to the condition:

```
if(
  ...
  message.manufacturer == Manufacturer.GARMIN.value 
):
  # update devive to Garmin Edge 830
```
ensures that Garmin Connect correctly identifies the uploaded activity as coming from a Garmin device — specifically, an Edge 830. This works reliably, regardless of what Garmin device metadata was originally in the file - it's changed to Edge 830.

Just wanted to ask if you think this might be a safe and reasonable to add or if it could have unintended side effects in other scenarios. I’d be happy to hear your thoughts.

Thanks again for your work on the project!

title: Cached authentication?
description:
Running on a Mac running 26.3 Beta (25D5087f).  

My wife and I both ride indoors this time of year and I wrote a wrapper script to swap out the .config.json file to copies created with our unique Garmin credentials and unique paths to each of our .fit files.  The first time I ran it with her credentials and path to her fit files, it uploaded everything to my Garmin account.  I had previously used the program successfully before making the wrapper script with my static credentials. 

I've added a few lines of logging statements within the app.py file to verify that when running the wrapper script it identifies her credentials, but still loading to my originally authenticated Garmin account.

I even tried putting completely unusable credentials in the .config.json file and everything logs showing that it's using the garbage details, but the file still uploads to my Garmin account.

Seems like Garth might be holding a cached authentication?

title: Support other FIT file sources
description:
With Zwift now considering outdoor rides for XP and streaks, this application becomes much more important...
TPVirtual will soon support Garmin Connect officially - this item is marked as planned on their uservoice feedback site.

However - the approach by this app can be applied to many other FIT file sources - for example, I have Coospo bike computer and would love to use that instead of buying Garmin and still earn XP for outdoor rides.

I tested this out - app accepts, process, modifies and uploads the Coospo produced fit file, it shows up in Zwift, but does not earn XP. TPVirtual ride FIT file, on the other hand - does.

Looking at the `_modified.fit` file, I see that File ID is not set to Garmin in Coospo ride.

I would think, it should be possible to construct valid FIT file which Garmin would accept as coming from its device as long as minimal necessary data is available in the source FIT...

Would you be willing to review this approach and make the app to support wide sources?
